title: 1.1 Python fluency beyond the basics
description: Roadmap 1.1 — 12 topics, in the document's own order.
learningOutcomes: Take every topic in this section to pass 3 of the roadmap's rule: intuition, then derived on paper, then implemented from scratch.

lessons.title: Data model: __dunder__ methods, descriptors, __slots__
learningObjectives: Explain why special methods are looked up on the type and not the instance, and predict what that breaks
Implement the equality, hashing and ordering contracts correctly, including the trap that makes a class unhashable
Write a data descriptor and explain where it sits in attribute lookup precedence
Decide when __slots__ is worth it, and name three things it takes away
lessons.description: How Python's object protocol actually works — special-method lookup on the type, the equality/hash contract, descriptors as the mechanism under properties and ORMs, and what __slots__ really buys you.

lessons.title: Iterators, generators, yield from, lazy evaluation
learningObjectives: Distinguish an iterable from an iterator and explain why the difference causes the exhaustion bug
Write generators that hold state across suspensions, and know what yield from forwards that a loop does not
Predict when laziness saves memory, when it defers an error, and when it holds a resource open too long
Compose itertools pipelines and name the two functions that quietly break the memory guarantee
lessons.description: The iterator protocol, generators as suspendable functions, yield from and delegation, and the real trade-offs of laziness — memory, single-pass exhaustion, deferred errors and resource lifetime.

lessons.title: Decorators, closures, functools (lru_cache, partial, wraps)
learningObjectives: Explain what a closure captures, why it captures a variable rather than a value, and how to fix the late-binding bug
Desugar any decorator by hand, including stacked and parameterised ones, and predict the order they run in
Use functools.wraps correctly and name what is still broken without it
Choose between lru_cache, cache and cached_property, and state the memory and correctness traps of each
lessons.description: Closures as cells over an enclosing frame, decorators as the plain function application they actually are, and the functools toolkit — wraps, lru_cache, partial, singledispatch, cached_property — with the failure mode each one brings.

lessons.title: Context managers and contextlib
learningObjectives: Desugar any with statement into its try/finally equivalent and predict exactly when __exit__ runs
Implement both the class-based and generator-based protocols, and say which one a given job wants
Explain what returning True from __exit__ does, and why almost every correct __exit__ returns None
Use ExitStack, suppress, nullcontext and asynccontextmanager where a plain with statement cannot reach
lessons.description: The with statement as a protocol you can implement, what __exit__ can and cannot do about an exception, and the contextlib toolkit — contextmanager, ExitStack, suppress, nullcontext — with the failure each one hides.

lessons.title: Type hints in depth: Generic, TypeVar, Protocol, Literal, overload
learningObjectives: Use TypeVar and generic syntax to preserve relationships between inputs, outputs, containers, and callback signatures
Design small Protocol contracts and explain structural subtyping, runtime_checkable limits, and variance at API boundaries
Use Literal, constrained and bounded type variables, ParamSpec, and Self only where each communicates a real invariant
Write sound overload sets whose variants match one runtime implementation, and recognise when a union or generic is clearer
lessons.description: Python typing as a language for preserving relationships: generics and TypeVar, structural Protocol contracts, Literal value domains, callable forwarding, variance, and honest overloads that match runtime behaviour.

lessons.title: dataclasses vs Pydantic v2 — when each is correct
learningObjectives: Explain why type annotations generate methods in a dataclass but drive runtime validation in a Pydantic model
Choose the correct model for trusted domain state, untrusted input, serialization, and JSON Schema generation
Configure coercion, strictness, extra fields, immutability, aliases, and validators deliberately in Pydantic v2
Keep validation at system boundaries and convert validated DTOs into dependency-light domain dataclasses
lessons.description: Choose dataclasses for trusted internal state and Pydantic v2 for untrusted boundaries, then design an explicit conversion point between them.

lessons.title: Exceptions, custom exception hierarchies, exception groups
learningObjectives: Trace exception matching, propagation, cleanup, chaining, and traceback preservation precisely
Design a small domain exception hierarchy that lets callers recover without parsing messages
Translate low-level failures at architectural boundaries with explicit causes, notes, and useful context
Use ExceptionGroup and except* to handle independent concurrent failures without losing unmatched errors
lessons.description: Treat exceptions as a typed failure API: preserve causes and tracebacks, design recoverable domain hierarchies, and handle multiple independent failures safely with ExceptionGroup and except*.

lessons.title: asyncio: event loop, tasks, gather, semaphores, backpressure
learningObjectives: Explain how the event loop advances coroutines and identify code that blocks every task
Choose deliberately among direct await, create_task, gather, TaskGroup, wait, and as_completed
Preserve cancellation and design timeouts and cleanup as part of a task's public contract
Bound concurrency and queued work with semaphores and queues that express an overload policy
lessons.description: Build bounded async systems: understand cooperative scheduling, own task lifetimes, preserve cancellation, and turn overload into explicit backpressure instead of hidden memory growth.

lessons.title: Concurrency reality: GIL, multiprocessing, concurrent.futures, when to use which
learningObjectives: Distinguish concurrency from parallelism and predict when the default CPython GIL limits throughput
Choose threads, processes, or asyncio from waiting time, Python CPU time, native code, and data-transfer costs
Use Executor and Future APIs with explicit ownership, failure, cancellation, and shutdown policies
Design process-safe workloads around picklable boundaries, start methods, batching, and measurement
lessons.description: Choose Python concurrency from measured workload shape: understand what the GIL protects, when threads overlap useful work, and when process isolation costs less than it saves.

lessons.title: Packaging: uv, pyproject.toml, editable installs, dependency pinning
learningObjectives: Explain the roles of pyproject.toml, build backends, wheels, source distributions, environments, and lockfiles
Use uv to create, lock, sync, run, and build a project without confusing declared constraints with resolved versions
Choose dependency bounds and pinning policies appropriate to applications, reusable libraries, and published artifacts
Diagnose editable-install, import-layout, index, platform-marker, and reproducibility failures at their real boundary
lessons.description: Build reproducible Python projects by separating package metadata, environment resolution, editable development, and application locking into explicit contracts.

lessons.title: Testing: pytest fixtures, parametrize, mocking, property-based testing with hypothesis
learningObjectives: Structure pytest tests as clear arrange-act-assert specifications with fixture ownership and deterministic cleanup
Use parametrization to expose meaningful cases without hiding behavior or multiplying duplicate tests
Patch names at their lookup boundary and use autospecced mocks only where a real collaborator must be controlled
Design Hypothesis strategies and invariants that reveal, reproduce, and shrink edge cases ordinary examples miss
lessons.description: Design tests around observable contracts using pytest fixtures and parametrization, narrow boundary mocks, and Hypothesis properties that search and shrink the input space.

lessons.title: Tooling: ruff, mypy strict mode, pre-commit
learningObjectives: Configure Ruff linting and formatting as complementary checks with deliberate rule selection and safe fix policy
Adopt mypy strictness without hiding uncertainty behind Any, broad ignores, or untyped package boundaries
Configure pinned pre-commit hooks whose file scope, environments, stages, and CI behavior are explicit
Design one fast local and authoritative CI quality pipeline with reproducible versions and actionable failures
lessons.description: Turn formatting, linting, static typing, and repository hooks into one reproducible quality contract that developers and CI execute identically.
